title: fix(sse): resolve partial-JSON delimiter & token/event ordering in SSE streaming (OpenAI compat)
author: Jordan Kim
description:
Motivation: Streaming responses (SSE) in the OpenAI-compatibility layer can produce malformed partial-JSON payloads or emit token/event fragments in an order that breaks consumer JSON parsers and function/tool-calling clients. This PR fixes three related issues: 1) delimiter handling when messages are split across network frames, 2) partial-JSON assembly when the payload boundary falls in the middle of an object/array, and 3) ordering of token/event boundary events which could cause `partial_json` consumers to see invalid sequences.

Summary of changes (single continuous description): Consolidated framing logic in redwood/openai_compat/sse.py to use a small state machine that tracks delimiter state across frames, introduced explicit buffer flush points for complete JSON token boundaries, added a re-ordering guard that ensures token 'event' and 'data' parts are emitted in the contract order required by the OpenAI streaming spec, and added regression tests covering truncated delimiters, multi-frame partial objects, and simultaneous token+event emit scenarios. Also included a small change to the streaming router (redwood/api/streaming.py) to prefer atomic message boundaries for high-priority streams under burst load.

Checklist:
- [x] Reproduce failing scenarios with unit/integration tests
- [x] Add deterministic fuzz-tests that simulate split frames/delimiters
- [x] Ensure backwards-compatible behavior for existing clients
- [x] Add trace logs gated behind debug flag for future incidents
- [x] Run performance benchmark to validate no regression on p50/p95

Testing: Added unit tests and an integration test harness (redwood-tests/test_sse_streaming.py) that exercise: (a) messages with delimiters split across TCP frames, (b) partial JSON objects split between frames, (c) interleaved token and event fragments. CI reproduced a flake during initial runs; I fixed the race in the test harness and re-ran. Final CI status: passing.

Rollout and migration notes: This is a bugfix for the OpenAI compatibility layer only; no API changes. The fix is safe to deploy on hosted and dedicated backends. For private installers, the change will be included in the next patch release. Observability: added a metric `sse.partial_json_errors` (debug-level) and a debug trace that emits when a fragment boundary is corrected.

Related: ENG-4821 (SSE partial-JSON incidents), ENG-4870 (token-event ordering regression), SUP-1123 (customer incident involving tool-calling payload failure).

review_thread:
Asha Patel (reviewer): Found a race where buffer flush could double-emit a final delimiter in high-traffic scenarios. Suggested adding an idempotent guard.
Jordan Kim (author): Addressed with an atomic flag around flush; added unit test.
Miguel Alvarez (reviewer): Asked for explicit coverage for function/tool-calling payloads that rely on closed JSON objects mid-stream.
Jordan Kim (author): Added integration case that reproduces the SUP-1123 customer failure and validated tool-calling path remains stable.
Lena Vogel (reviewer): Requested clearer debug traces and a metric to help on-call triage.
Jordan Kim (author): Added `sse.partial_json_errors` metric and debug trace gated by `REDWOOD_DEBUG_SSE`.
Post-approval: CI failed once due to a flaky test harness; reran CI after test fix. Final status: 2 approvals (Asha Patel, Miguel Alvarez) and merged via squash.
release_notes: Fixes SSE streaming partial-JSON framing and token/event ordering that could produce malformed streaming payloads in OpenAI compatibility mode. Improves reliability of tool/function-calling over streaming and adds regression tests. No API change.
